- **Member Onboarding** – first 7 days, first class experience, induction checklist, liability waivers, payment setup, goal-setting call. *Why critical: determines retention trajectory; every delay compounds churn risk.*
- **Member Pause/Cancellation/Churn** – pause request workflow, billing pause, re-engagement trigger points, exit interview capture, win-back sequences. *Why critical: predictable revenue leakage; no documented decision tree means ad-hoc handling.*

- **Member Data Privacy & GDPR** – data collection consent flows, retention/deletion timelines, DPA compliance for contact/payment data, member data access requests, breach protocol. *Why critical: legal exposure; especially acute with female-only member base and biometric/health data.*

# Service Menu Execution for The Forge

**1. Start with your coaches — they're your source of truth**
Run a 30-min workshop with your coaching team. Ask: "What do we actually sell?" (Not what you think you sell — what they deliver daily). Capture every service variant they currently mention: group classes, 1-on-1 packages, nutrition add-ons, form checks, progress tracking. This reveals what's *already* generating value.

**2. Price by outcome, not time**
Don't list "60-min session = £40." Instead: "6-week strength foundation package (2x weekly + form videos) = £X." Women buy transformation, not minutes. Test pricing on your most recent members — ask what they'd pay for the exact outcome they got. Use that data.

**3. Create two separate menus — literally different documents**
**Coach menu:** Lists every service with profit margins, time commitment, and upsell triggers (e.g., "When member hits 4 weeks, mention nutrition audit"). **Member menu:** Clean, benefit-focused, no jargon. Show what problem each service solves ("Nutrition audit: Stop guessing what actually works for *your* body").

**4. Hardcode this into your booking system TODAY**
Don't create a PDF and file it. Build it into your gym's booking/CRM system so coaches see the full menu when a member books. Friction kills upsells — make it frictionless for them to suggest the right next step.

**5. Test it for 2 weeks with one coach**
Pick your most adaptable coach. Have her use the new menu structure with 10 members. Track which services actually convert and which

## REVENUE TRENDS & ALERTS

**What's off-track:**
- **Revenue per member collapsed from £145 (July) → £103 (Oct).** You're adding members (120→173) but revenue/head is down 29% in 3 months. This is your biggest red flag.
- **Last 3 months avg £17,320 vs prior 3 months avg £17,668.** Flat-to-declining despite 30 more members. The studio expansion isn't yet translating to revenue lift.
- **Churn spiked to 12.8% in May** (relocation month — understandable) but you're still at 3.9–6.2%, which is acceptable. That's not the problem.

**The problem is pricing or membership mix:**
- Either new members are on cheaper tiers, or existing members aren't upgrading to classes/PT/merchandise.
- **Action 1: Audit your membership tiers.** What % are on the base tier vs premium (classes + PT credits + retail)? Target: shift 15% of base-tier members to premium within 60 days. Premium should carry at least 40% margin lift vs entry tier. Use email + 1-to-1 outreach.
- **Action 2: Introduce a class pass upsell.** New 10-class bundles (no membership) at £89–99. Retention is only good if members *use* the studio. Quiet class slots (early morning, late evening, mid-week) should have a "fill-the-class" discount: existing members + 3 friends for £25/head. Track attendance by time; move weak classes.
- **Action 3: Launch a PT/nutrition membership add-on.** Even 10% uptake at +£25/month per member = +£400/month (at 162 members). Personal training and body comp tracking are high-margin, and women-only is a selling point.
